title: How would you estimate the yearly revenue of all car washes in the US?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "What is the yearly revenue of all car washes in the US?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A value question that combines a big base (vehicles) with a frequency (washes a year) and a price. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

What is the yearly revenue of all car washes in the US?

The approach

Vehicles × professional washes per year × average price.

Tip: Round to friendly numbers and say that you are rounding. Nobody expects decimals.

Step by step

  1. Vehicles in the US: 290M
  2. × 3 professional washes per vehicle per year
  3. × $15 average price

That gives about $13.1B a year.

Does it make sense?

About $45 per vehicle per year: one wash every four months.

Distinguish paid washes from every time a car gets clean

The market estimate concerns professional car-wash revenue, not washing at home. Cars driven heavily, especially ride-hailing and fleet vehicles, may be washed much more often than privately owned cars. A simple segment mix can improve the assumption.

Suppose 80% of vehicles buy two washes a year and 20% buy seven. That averages three annual paid washes per vehicle, agreeing with the original assumption. At 290 million vehicles and $15 each, the resulting market is approximately $13.05 billion. The split helps you see why fleet behaviour matters.

Be careful with subscriptions: an unlimited-wash member may visit often but pay a fixed monthly fee. Multiplying visits by a single price can overstate revenue. If subscription washes are material, estimate subscriber count × monthly fee × twelve separately from pay-per-wash purchases.
